abstract: Pigs are important agricultural resources and valuable biomedical models, necessitating a high-quality pan-genome to comprehensively capture genomic diversity. Here we present an extensive genomic and phenotypic resource comprising 3 telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genomes and 16 high-quality assemblies. This resource enables the construction of the pig pan-transcriptome and pan-metabolome, thereby enhancing genotype-phenotype mapping. Using 12 Y-chromosome assemblies, we resolved centromere repositioning at basepair resolution, establishing centromeres as unique evolutionary markers. Reconstruction of centromeric three-dimensional genomic architecture revealed their role as structural scaffolds that concentrate chromatin interactions. We identified eEF1A1, a transcriptionally active gene consistently located near chromosome 1 centromeres, as a candidate hotspot for karyotype variation. From a pan-structural variation map, we pinpointed AKR1B1 as a key gene underlying hypoxia adaptation. Moreover, a graph-based pan-genome built from T2T genomes improved heritability capture. Together, this work provides a foundation for studies of centromere evolution, adaptive genetics and precision breeding.
